root_cause: exportFinancialReport<T extends Record<string, unknown>> used a single T for all sections, so TypeScript inferred the heterogeneous sections array ({rev:number} vs {exp:number}) as a union of incompatible types.
decision: Relaxed the function signature in AdvancedExcelEngine.ts (line 120) to allow heterogeneous sections using Record<string, unknown> for data and string for column keys. Test data is semantically correct (Revenue/Expenses are different schemas), and the function body already handles string-keyed access into unknown data, so the constraint added no runtime value.

change.before: static exportFinancialReport<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(report: { title: string; sections: Array<{ name: string; data: T[]; columns: Array<{ header: string; key: Extract<keyof T, string> }>; }>; }): Blob
change.after: static exportFinancialReport(report: { title: string; sections: Array<{ name: string; data: Record<string, unknown>[]; columns: Array<{ header: string; key: string }>; }>; }): Blob

side_effects: No other callers of exportFinancialReport in src/. Signature relaxation matches the function body's actual semantics (string-keyed access into unknown data). Remaining 6 tsc errors are in App.tsx/DepreciationPage/DashboardPage and unrelated to this fix.
